cleanIntro: ⛔ This pistol strips on PULL-DOWN TABS, one on each side of the frame, and the trigger MUST be pulled as part of the sequence — Kimber says so in a note above the procedure. The order is strict and it is not guessable: slide back a quarter inch, tabs down, slide forward, THEN the trigger.

steps.title: Unloaded and inspected — and yes, the trigger gets pulled
steps.action: Magazine out, chamber confirmed empty by eye, muzzle safe throughout. ⛔ Read the note first: pulling the trigger IS part of this strip, which is why the unload check is not a formality here — it is the only thing standing between the procedure and a discharge.
steps.aside: Exercise great caution as the recoil spring is under tension and can fly out with enough force to cause serious injury, property damage or loss.
steps.quote: Pulling the trigger is required for disassembly of the R7 Mako.
steps.cite: Kimber R7 Mako Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — Disassembly (Field Stripping) & Assembly

steps.title: Slide back a QUARTER INCH and hold it there
steps.action: Grip the slide and the frame and pull the slide rearward about a quarter of an inch — just out of battery — and hold it. Too far and the tabs will not move; not far enough and they will not either.
steps.quote: Using your dominant hand, grip the slide and frame and pull the slide rearward 1/4 inch until the slide is partially out of battery. Hold the slide in this position.
steps.cite: Kimber R7 Mako Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — Disassembly (Field Stripping) & Assembly

steps.title: Both pull-down tabs DOWN, then let the slide forward
steps.action: With your support hand, find the pull-down tab on BOTH sides of the frame, take them between thumb and forefinger and pull them downward. Keep them down while you let the slide run forward.
steps.aside: While pulling the tabs down allow the slide to go forward while maintaining the downward hold on the pull-down tabs.
steps.quote: Using your support hand, locate the pull-down tab visible on both sides of the frame and grasp them with your thumb and forefinger and pull the tab downward.
steps.cite: Kimber R7 Mako Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — Disassembly (Field Stripping) & Assembly

steps.title: ⛔ Now the trigger — muzzle safe, chamber proven empty
steps.action: With the muzzle in a safe direction, pull the trigger. That disengages the striker from the trigger bar sear surface and it is the step the whole strip hinges on. Then take your fingers off the tabs and push the slide forward another quarter inch.
steps.quote: use your dominant hand and pull the trigger. This will disengage the striker from the trigger bar sear surface.
steps.cite: Kimber R7 Mako Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — Disassembly (Field Stripping) & Assembly

steps.title: Slide STRAIGHT UP off the rails, then spring and barrel
steps.action: Lift the slide straight UP off the rails — not forward. Then take the recoil spring assembly out by pushing the rear of the guide rod toward the muzzle, lifting slightly, and pulling it back and out of the rear of the slide. Barrel last. Strip complete.
steps.aside: Remove the recoil spring assembly by pushing on the rear of the recoil spring guide rod towards the muzzle and lifting slightly.
steps.quote: Lift the slide straight up off of the rails.
steps.cite: Kimber R7 Mako Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — Disassembly (Field Stripping) & Assembly

steps.title: ⛔ Rod in from the CHAMBER end, every time
steps.action: The cleaning rod enters at the chamber, never the muzzle. Wet patch with bore solvent, let it soak a few minutes, dry patch to lift the loose debris — and read the solvent maker's own directions, because some of them will lift a finish as happily as they lift fouling.
steps.aside: Run a patch wet with bore cleaning solvent through the barrel and let the solution soak a few minutes.
steps.quote: Always insert a cleaning rod from the chamber end of the barrel.
steps.cite: Kimber R7 Mako Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — CLEANING

steps.title: Wet brush through and OUT the muzzle, then repeat to clean
steps.action: Push the wet bore brush in at the chamber and all the way OUT of the muzzle before drawing it back — reversing a brush inside the bore folds the bristles over. Dry patch after, and repeat the pair until a patch comes out clean. Then a light oil, and ⛔ a dry patch through before you ever fire it.
steps.aside: Run a dry patch through the barrel before firing to remove oil.
steps.quote: Run a wet bore brush through the chamber end of the barrel and out the muzzle, making several passes.
steps.cite: Kimber R7 Mako Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — CLEANING

steps.title: Breech face and every bearing surface — nylon brush
steps.action: Wipe the dirt off all the bearing surfaces on the slide and frame, then get into the breech face and the rest of the parts with a toothbrush or similar nylon brush. ⛔ And no ultrasonic tank: Kimber says damage from one is not covered by warranty, and night sights must never go near it.
steps.aside: Do not expose night sights to an ultrasonic cleaning environment.
steps.quote: Clean the breech face and all parts (a toothbrush or similar nylon brush works well).
steps.cite: Kimber R7 Mako Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — CLEANING

steps.title: Lubricate by the drop, at the points Kimber names
steps.action: Premium oil, not grease — and if it carries Teflon, shake it, because the Teflon settles overnight and you will otherwise apply the carrier and none of the additive. Then oil only where this book says, in the quantities it gives.
steps.aside: Outside of barrel; 3 drops spread across surface
steps.quote: Slide and frame rails; 3 drops on each side
steps.cite: Kimber R7 Mako Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — LUBRICATION

steps.title: ⛔ Nothing in the firing pin channel, and wipe the excess
steps.action: Reassemble, work the slide five or six times, dry fire, then wipe off the excess. Moderation is the whole point: too little and it wears, too much and it collects the grit that wears it faster. ⛔ And if it has been stored oiled, a dry patch goes through the barrel before firing.
steps.quote: If the firearm has been stored with oil in the barrel and chamber, push a dry patch through the barrel before firing.
steps.cite: Kimber R7 Mako Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — LUBRICATION

deepAbsentReason: Kimber's limit is printed in the strip itself — "The firearm is now disassembled. No further disassembly is required for general cleaning." — and again as a warning: "Do not disassemble your firearm beyond field stripping outlined in this manual. Do not manipulate any internal components beyond what you are instructed to do in this manual." Going further voids the warranty in Kimber's own words. A manufacturer's published DON'T outranks every other tier, so nothing deeper is authored from anywhere else.

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: ⛔ Rod ALWAYS from the chamber end
Wet patch, soak a few minutes, dry patch
Wet brush in at the chamber and OUT the muzzle before drawing back
Repeat until a patch comes out clean, then a light oil

cleaning.name: SLIDE & FRAME
tasks: Breech face and parts with a nylon brush
⛔ No ultrasonic cleaning — the damage is not warranted

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION
tasks: Premium oil, NOT grease; shake it if it contains Teflon
Only the points this model's book names, in the drops it gives
⛔ Never into the firing pin channel
Work the slide 5-6 times, dry fire, wipe the excess off

cleaning.name: MAGAZINES
tasks: Wiped clean; follower checked to slide freely

reassembly: Barrel into the slide, thread protector back on if it has one.
Recoil spring assembly in from the rear of the slide, guide rod nose into its seat.
Slide lowered STRAIGHT DOWN onto the frame rails and run back until it locks.
⛔ Confirm both pull-down tabs are back up and flush before the slide is released under spring pressure.
Cycle the slide, dry fire, wipe off excess lubrication.
fncheck: Reassembled and unloaded: work the slide five or six times and confirm it returns fully into battery, then dry fire and wipe the excess oil off. Check both pull-down tabs have returned flush — a tab left down is a slide that can come off the rails.
